hits.subject: polymaker-polyterra-pla-plus
hits.title: PolyTerra PLA+ technical data sheet V5.1 (Polymaker)
hits.section: How it differs from the plain grade
hits.text:
The sheet says "PolyTerra™ PLA+ filament contains organic material than ordinary PLA which brings
better layer adhesion and extra toughness." The source text reads this way, without a comparative
before "organic material".

hits.subject: water
hits.title: Study and Interpretation of the Chemical Characteristics of Natural Water (Hem, USGS Water-Supply Paper 1473)
hits.text:
Fresh water density is close to 1 gram per millilitre, and it depends on temperature and on what
is dissolved. The report says "The density is usually determined to three decimal places, and the
temperature at which it was made (usually 20°C) is given." It also says "The density of a water is
a significant physical property that affects its behavior in natural systems".

hits.subject: water
hits.title: Study and Interpretation of the Chemical Characteristics of Natural Water (Hem, USGS Water-Supply Paper 1473)
hits.text:

content.text:
I couldn't find the density of Bambu Lab PLA Basic in the knowledge base. Two searches ("Bambu Lab PLA Basic density" and "Bambu PLA Basic filament technical data sheet") returned no Bambu Lab sources. They only turned up other materials:

- **Polymaker PolyTerra PLA (plain grade):** "1.31g/cm3 at 23°C". Source: *PolyTerra PLA technical data sheet V6.0* (Polymaker), p. 1, Density section.
- **Polymaker PolyTerra PLA+ (toughened grade):** "Density ISO1183, GB/T1033 1.24 g/cm3 at 21.5°C". Source: *PolyTerra PLA+ technical data sheet V5.1* (Polymaker), p. 2.
- Water references from a USGS report, which don't apply here.

Both of these are different products from a different maker, and they differ from each other by about 5%. So neither one is a reliable stand-in for Bambu Lab PLA Basic, and I won't give you a number I can't cite.

You could get the figure from Bambu Lab's own technical data sheet for PLA Basic, on their website or wiki. If you share it, or tell me to go ahead with one of the Polymaker values as a stated approximation, I can use it. If you plan to score a part for mass, I can also check whether the materials table has a key for Bambu PLA Basic. It lists names only, not densities.

- Water references from a USGS report, which don't apply here.
